issue: The dataset described a network but never analysed it
correction: 56 nodes with centrality, cut-point status and node-removal impact, every metric computed twice
reason: Every figure is given over the topology the register states AND over the topology the dataset can draw. Reporting only the drawable graph would claim the network is broken where in fact the data is; reporting only the stated graph would overstate what the dataset supports. The difference between them is the uncertainty caused by the five unlocated nodes.
source: pipeline_edges.csv + pipeline_nodes.csv; algorithms cross-checked against networkx

issue: Hand-written Brandes betweenness was exactly 2x the correct value
correction: Uran 0.2323
reason: On an undirected graph Brandes visits every pair from both ends, so the accumulated score must be halved before normalising. No rank changed, so the printed report looked correct; found only by the independent networkx cross-check in 15_validate_vulnerability.py.
source: networkx betweenness_centrality(normalized=True), agreement now within 1e-6

issue: Treating pipelines that share a place name as physically connected is an inference the register never states
correction: stated on every row of both vulnerability tables
reason: Uran is named by four pipelines, so the graph has them meeting there. If any pair passes through without a tie-in, the graph contains a connection that does not exist and every centrality figure shifts. Recorded as the largest threat to this step's validity.
source: README 8.10

issue: node_geocode_review.csv was published in data_processed/ with none of its 26 columns described, while the README and the manuscript both state that every published column is described in the dictionary. The claim was false and no check tested it.
original: 226 rows covering 16 of the 17 published data files
correction: 252 rows covering all 17. The 19 columns node_geocode_review.csv shares with pipeline_nodes.csv are copied verbatim from those entries so the two cannot drift; the 7 columns unique to the review file are newly described.
reason: An undocumented published file is an unusable published file. The shared columns were copied rather than rewritten so that a future edit to one description cannot leave the other stale.
source: data_processed/node_geocode_review.csv headers; every factual claim in the new descriptions asserted against the file before writing (9 rows carry an alias note, 5 have no coordinate, 10 have no legacy corroborating point)

issue: Nothing tested the dictionary against the data, which is why the gap above survived 215 passing checks and five closure proofs
correction: New validator. Compares dictionary and headers in BOTH directions: every published column documented, every documented column published, column orders agreeing, every provenance_category in {A, B, C}, no duplicate (file, column) pair. Reads headers only and alters nothing.
reason: The 215 data checks all verify values. None verified that the metadata describing those values was complete. A claim a reader is asked to trust must be testable by the reader.
source: metadata/data_dictionary.csv vs the real headers of data_processed/*.csv

issue: The inventory listed four files that are not in the record, three of them marked COMPLETE. Most serious: data_raw/20251231_NGPL.pdf, which is deliberately not redistributed. A reviewer who cloned the record and ran 10_validate_master.py got INCOMPLETE rather than the 44/44 the same README advertises, with no explanation.
original: 20251231_NGPL.pdf COMPLETE; external/gazetteer/ COMPLETE; osm_pipelines_raw.geojson reference; pipeline_buffer_5km.geojson pending. Three further data_processed entries marked pending also did not exist.
correction: Contents lists only files in the record. New section 9.1 names the three inputs the scripts retrieve rather than redistribute, where each goes, how to get it and which step needs it, and states that INCOMPLETE from step 10 without the PDF is correct behaviour. New section 9.2 names what is not included in this version and why.
reason: Advertising an absent file is worse than omitting it: the reader cannot tell a licensing decision from a packaging mistake, and a validator refusing to run looks like a broken record rather than a working gate.
source: Package contents compared file by file against the section 9 listing

issue: The record was published with the release metadata unfilled. CITATION.cff carried [YOUR-GITHUB-USERNAME], [ZENODO DOI - add after first release], [FAMILY NAME], [GIVEN NAMES], [AFFILIATION] and [YOUR ORCID]; LICENSE carried [AUTHOR NAME]; README section 11 said the licence and citation were 'to be set before release'. All of it was visible to anyone who opened the repository.
original: six placeholders in CITATION.cff, one in LICENSE, version 1.0.0, no DOI
correction: repository-code, doi (10.5281/zenodo.22879173), version 2.0.0, creator and affiliation filled; orcid omitted rather than filled with a placeholder; LICENSE copyright filled; README section 11 states both licences and the citation. CITATION.cff carries a comment requiring its creator list to match the Zenodo record and any paper's dataset reference.
reason: Unfilled placeholders in a citation file make the record uncitable and signal that it was not checked before release. The creator list is left at one name because that is what the live Zenodo record states; the two must be changed together or not at all.
source: Live Zenodo record for 10.5281/zenodo.22879173; affiliation as printed in the manuscript

issue: The README credited 10_validate_master.py with 13 caught mutations and printed the mutation table twice, the first copy truncated after two rows. No --mutate harness for that script exists anywhere in the record, so the figure could not be reproduced by a reader. A total of 57 mutations was carried into the accompanying article on the strength of it.
original: 10_validate_master.py 13/13; four validators, 57 mutations in total; table duplicated
correction: The 13 is withdrawn, not restated. The table now lists what ships: 14, 15, 15 and 8 mutations for scripts 12, 13, 15 and 17, all re-runnable with --mutate, 52 in total. Scripts 10 and 11 are listed with no count and a note that mutation testing shaped them but no harness was kept; both of the specific findings are quoted from the code. The duplicate table is removed.
reason: An unreproducible count is worse in this record than no count, because the whole claim of the package is that a reader can re-run what it asserts. The two findings that mutation testing produced in scripts 10 and 11 are real and are documented in the code, so they are reported as findings rather than as a score.
source: grep for --mutate across scripts/ returns 12, 13, 15 and 17 only; comments at 10_validate_master.py group 7 and 11_validate_nodes.py above group 5
